title: ICSE CLASS 5 — English | Direct Indirect Speech
description: Subject-wise test on Direct Indirect Speech (English) for ICSE CLASS 5. 25Q.
subject: icse5-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect speech for the sentence: 'The teacher said, "The Earth revolves around the Sun."'?

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
options.explanation: The tense should remain unchanged for general truths.

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
options.explanation: Correct, as the tense remains unchanged for a general truth.

options.text: The teacher said the Earth revolves around the Sun.
options.explanation: The conjunction 'that' is often used in indirect speech for clarity.

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth is revolving around the Sun.
options.explanation: The present continuous tense is incorrect for a general truth.

questions.explanation: When reporting a general truth or fact, the tense remains unchanged in indirect speech. The Earth revolving around the Sun is a scientific fact, so the present simple tense is retained.
questions.hint: General truths retain their tense in indirect speech.
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech for the sentence: 'He said, "I have finished my homework."'

options.text: He said he finished his homework.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past perfect for sequence of tenses.

options.text: He said he had finished his homework.
options.explanation: Correct, as the present perfect changes to past perfect.

options.text: He said I had finished my homework.
options.explanation: The pronoun should remain consistent with the original speaker.

options.text: He said he has finished his homework.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past perfect in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the present perfect tense 'have finished' changes to past perfect 'had finished' to maintain the sequence of tenses.
questions.hint: Present perfect tense changes to past perfect in indirect speech.
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect speech for the sentence: 'She said, "I will visit my grandmother tomorrow."'?

options.text: She said she will visit her grandmother tomorrow.
options.explanation: The future tense should change to 'would' in indirect speech.

options.text: She said she would visit her grandmother the next day.
options.explanation: 'Tomorrow' should remain unchanged as it is a fixed time expression.

options.text: She said she would visit her grandmother tomorrow.
options.explanation: Correct, as 'will' changes to 'would' and 'tomorrow' remains unchanged.

options.text: She said she will visit her grandmother the next day.
options.explanation: Both the tense and time expression are incorrect.

questions.explanation: The future tense 'will' changes to 'would' in indirect speech. The word 'tomorrow' remains unchanged as it is a fixed time expression.
questions.hint: Future tense changes to 'would' in indirect speech.
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: Read the following sentence and choose the correct indirect speech: 'The shopkeeper said, "Are you looking for something special?"'

options.text: The shopkeeper asked if I was looking for something special.
options.explanation: Correct, as the interrogative is changed to a statement with 'was.'

options.text: The shopkeeper asked if I was looking for something special.
options.explanation: This is identical to option A and cannot be correct twice.

options.text: The shopkeeper asked was I looking for something special.
options.explanation: The word order should change to a statement in indirect speech.

options.text: The shopkeeper asked if I am looking for something special.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past ('was') to match the reporting verb.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, interrogative sentences are changed to statements. The auxiliary verb 'are' changes to 'was' to match the past tense of the reporting verb 'asked.'
questions.hint: Interrogative sentences change to statements in indirect speech.
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is correctly converted to indirect speech? Direct: 'Do you know the way to the station?' she asked.

options.text: She asked do I know the way to the station.
options.explanation: The word order should change to a statement in indirect speech.

options.text: She asked if I knew the way to the station?
options.explanation: The question mark should be removed in indirect speech.

options.text: She asked if I knew the way to the station.
options.explanation: Correct, as the interrogative changes to a statement with 'if' and past tense.

options.text: She asked that do I know the way to the station.
options.explanation: The structure 'that do' is incorrect for indirect speech.

questions.explanation: The interrogative sentence is converted to an assertive sentence in indirect speech. 'Do you know' changes to 'if I knew,' and the question mark is removed.
questions.hint: Interrogative sentences change to assertive sentences in indirect speech.
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: Assertion: In converting direct speech to indirect speech, the tense of the verb never changes. Reason: The tense changes only when the reported speech expresses a general truth.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.explanation: The assertion is false, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
options.explanation: The assertion is false, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
options.explanation: The assertion is false, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: Assertion is false, but Reason is true.
options.explanation: Correct, as the assertion is false and the reason is true but unrelated.

questions.explanation: The assertion is false because the tense often changes in indirect speech to maintain sequence of tenses. The reason is true but does not explain the assertion correctly.
questions.hint: Consider the rules of sequence of tenses in indirect speech.

options.explanation: Correct, as the present perfect continuous changes to past perfect continuous.

options.text: The student said he had studied for two hours.
options.explanation: The continuous aspect is lost in this option.

questions.question: What is the correct indirect speech for the sentence: 'The teacher said, "The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan."'?

questions.question: Case-based: Ravi said, 'I saw a lion in the zoo yesterday.' Which of the following is the correct indirect speech?

options.text: Ravi said he saw a lion in the zoo the day before.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past perfect ('had seen').

options.text: Ravi said he had seen a lion in the zoo yesterday.
options.explanation: 'Yesterday' should change to 'the day before' in indirect speech.

options.text: Ravi said he had seen a lion in the zoo the day before.
options.explanation: Correct, as the tense changes to past perfect and 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before.'

options.text: Ravi said he saw a lion in the zoo yesterday.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past perfect in indirect speech.

questions.explanation: The past simple tense 'saw' changes to past perfect 'had seen,' and 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before' in indirect speech. This maintains the sequence of tenses and correct time reference.
questions.hint: Past simple tense changes to past perfect, and 'yesterday' changes to 'the day before.'
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: What is the correct indirect speech for the sentence: 'The manager said, "All employees must submit their reports by Friday."'?

options.text: The manager said that all employees must submit their reports by Friday.
options.explanation: Correct, as 'must' remains unchanged and 'that' is used.

options.text: The manager said that all employees had to submit their reports by Friday.
options.explanation: 'Must' is preferred over 'had to' when the obligation is still in force.

options.text: The manager said all employees must submit their reports by Friday.
options.explanation: The conjunction 'that' is often used for clarity in indirect speech.

options.text: The manager said that all employees would have to submit their reports by Friday.
options.explanation: 'Would have to' is incorrect as 'must' is still in force.

questions.explanation: The modal verb 'must' remains unchanged in indirect speech when it expresses a rule or obligation that is still in force. The conjunction 'that' is used to introduce the reported speech.
questions.hint: Modal verbs like 'must' often remain unchanged in indirect speech for rules or obligations.
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: The teacher said, 'The sun rises in the east.' What is the correct indirect speech?

options.text: The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.

options.text: The teacher said that the sun rises in the east.
options.explanation: Correct, as the tense remains unchanged for universal facts.

options.text: The teacher said that the sun is rising in the east.
options.explanation: The tense should not change to present continuous for universal facts.

options.text: The teacher said that the sun has risen in the east.
options.explanation: The tense should not change to present perfect for universal facts.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, the tense remains unchanged when the statement is still true or a universal fact. 'Rises' remains 'rises' in indirect speech.

questions.question: He said, 'I am reading a book.' What is the correct indirect speech form?

options.text: He said that I was reading a book.
options.explanation: The pronoun 'I' should change to 'he' to match the speaker.

options.text: He said that he was reading a book.
options.explanation: Correct, as the pronoun 'I' changes to 'he'.

options.text: He said that he is reading a book.
options.explanation: The tense should change to past continuous in indirect speech.

options.text: He said that I am reading a book.
options.explanation: Both the pronoun and tense are incorrect.

questions.explanation: In indirect speech, pronouns and possessives must change according to the subject. 'I' changes to 'he' to match the speaker.
questions.hint: Pronouns must agree with the subject of the reporting sentence.
questions.subject: icse5-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): In indirect speech, the word 'said' can be replaced with 'told' only if the object is mentioned. Reason (R): 'Told' requires a person as an object (e.g., 'He told me').

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true, and R is also true.

questions.explanation: 'Told' must be followed by a person (e.g., 'He told me...'), so R correctly explains A.
questions.hint: Consider the grammatical rules for using 'said' and 'told' in indirect speech.

questions.question: The doctor said, 'Take this medicine twice a day.' What is the indirect speech form?

options.text: The doctor told that take this medicine twice a day.
options.explanation: 'Told' should be followed by an object (e.g., 'told me').

questions.explanation: Commands or instructions in direct speech are reported using 'advise + to-infinitive' in indirect speech.
